<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
Adds Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock.forward_cp for callers that hold a row-sharded hidden state: gate and top-k run on the local rows, then the rows and their top-k ids/weights are all-gathered together so the TP-sharded experts still see every token, and the partial sum is reduce-scattered back to the local rows. Same bytes on the wire as the all-reduce of the TP path, plus 80 B per token for the top-k payload.

The two collectives are injected as callables, so this carries no dependency on any particular CP layout.

Routing uses the fused topk_softmax + build_precomputed_topk_output rather than a second TopK module: the Triton router costs ~0.2 ms of host time per layer, which is +10 ms on a 4K forward. That yields the STANDARD top-k format, so the FlashInfer TRT-LLM runner picks its routed kernels from the top-k format instead of asserting BYPASSED -- switching the model to flashinfer_trtllm_routed instead would also change the TP path's routing numerics.

Measured per MoE layer on 4x B200: gate GEMM 70 -> 11 us, routing 51 -> 17 us (~4.5 ms per 32K forward), all-gather launch count unchanged.

@@ -177,6 +177,40 @@ Compute cooperates through the flags the scope publishes on `get_forward()`:
 
 A complete tensor after `finish()` can still have a pending **residual update**. An incomplete reduction is exposed to the model as an opaque `OwedOutput`; pass it to the next boundary or a supported access method. Do not inspect it as a tensor, slice it, or unwrap its contribution in model code.
 
+### Route locally before a CP gather
+
+For a sparse FFN that routes tokens before gathering them, use `declare_ffn(sparse=True, gathers_cp_input=True)`. This capability applies only to the context-parallel batch variant. It supports TP-only MoE with collocated prefill CP: CP and MoE TP cover the same ordered ranks, attention TP/DP and MoE EP/DP are one, and all-to-all and DWDP are disabled. Ordinary batches retain their existing input and output behavior.
+
+The boundary prepares the input on CP-local rows and retains the local residual. Compute runs the gate and top-k locally, gathers hidden states and routing payload together, and runs the experts on the gathered rows. Every gathered tensor must use the same rank-major blocks, padded to the maximum count in `forward_batch.attn_cp_metadata.per_rank_actual_token`. The MoE returns a partial output for all padded rows. It must not call `reduce_moe_output()`, run an output collective, or reshape the output to the local row count itself.
+
+The exit owns both the reduction and the return to local rows. With a reduce-scatter policy, it sums the partial expert outputs and removes collective padding. With an all-reduce policy, the exit completes the sum before taking back the local rows. Compute returns the same partial output under either policy. An update with `applied_at_exit=True` runs after this movement, so a nonlinear residual update sees a complete contribution on its residual's rows. `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock.forward_cp()` provides the compute path; a caller must select it only for the active CP variant and supply the matching gather and allocation callbacks.
+
+After opting into the declaration, select this path from the boundary's actual input rows. This also respects batches using sequence parallelism or scattered attention input:
+
+```python
+from sglang.srt.layers.layer_boundary import TokenAxis
+
+hidden_states = self.ffn_boundary.prepare(hidden_states, forward_batch)
+cp_local = (
+    TokenAxis.ATTN_CP
+    in self.ffn_boundary.entry(forward_batch).input_rows.sharded
+)
+with self.ffn_boundary.exit(forward_batch) as output:
+    if cp_local:
+        hidden_states = self.mlp.forward_cp(
+            hidden_states,
+            all_gather_rows=all_gather_rows,
+            symmetric_memory=symmetric_memory,
+        )
+    else:
+        hidden_states = self.mlp(hidden_states, forward_batch=forward_batch)
+hidden_states = output.finish(hidden_states)
+```
+
+The gather callback must run even on empty local ranks and zero-pad hidden states, routing weights, and expert IDs to the same rank-block size. The CUDA Qwen helper calls the existing `select_experts()` on local rows and gathers its STANDARD IDs and weights. It requires a runner accepting that format, such as the FlashInfer TRT-LLM routed kernels. Normal token-wise scoring, bias, expert grouping, and scaling remain available without a separate CP router implementation.
+
+This path requires trivial expert placement with no redundant experts, EPLB, expert-distribution recording, or routed-expert capture. The Qwen constructor supplies a token-wise router; simulated routing is excluded because it depends on global row indices. Topology validation and reduction policy belong to the boundary.
+
 ### Enter and leave the layer stack
 
 Initialize a fresh stream once on the embedding path, and leave the stack through the final norm:
